facts.text: Żoliborz means "Beautiful Embankment," a name borrowed from the French Joli Bord and later Polishized.
During the 1944 Warsaw Uprising, Żoliborz was one of the first districts to rise, yet it escaped the widespread destruction that befell the city.
The 1831 Warsaw Citadel, once a Russian fortress, now shelters the 10th Pavilion Museum, the Katyń Museum, and the Museum of Polish History.
Just a 15‑minute walk from Wilsona Square lies the Olympic Centre, home to the Museum of Sport and Tourism and a collection of Olympic medals.
Żoliborz’s streets showcase 1930s modernist villas, many built for officers and journalists, reflecting the district’s early 20th‑century elite character.
Polish rock legend Czesław Niemen, film director Andrzej Wajda, and actress Zofia Merle all called Żoliborz home at some point.
